It was a tremendous blow to him. But I don't know why he should have made such a fuss about it, seeing that he had done the same--practically the same--himself.

69964-history-of-the-war-in-the-peninsul.title: History Of The War In The Peninsula And In The South Of Fran
69964-history-of-the-war-in-the-peninsul.creator: Unknown
69964-history-of-the-war-in-the-peninsul.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Lord Wellington blockades Pampeluna, besieges St. Sebastian—Operations on the eastern coast of Spain—General Elio’s   misconduct—Sir John Murray sails to attack Taragona—Colonel Prevot   takes St. Felippe de Balaguer—Second siege of Taragona—Suchet and   Maurice Mathieu endeavour to relieve the place—Sir John Murray   raises the siege—Embarks with the loss of his guns—Disembarks again   at St. Felippe de Balaguer—Lord William Bentinck arrives—Sir John   Murray’s trial—Observations Page 1

arxiv-1611-05428.title: Upscaledb: Efficient Integer-Key Compression in a Key-Value Store using SIMD Instructions Journal: Information Systems
arxiv-1611-05428.creator: Daniel Lemire, Christoph Rupp
arxiv-1611-05428.description: Abstract Compression can sometimes improve performance by making more of the data available to the processors faster. We consider the compression of integer keys in a B+-tree index. For this purpose, systems such as IBM DB2 use variable-byte compression over differentially coded keys. We revisit this problem with various compression alternatives such as Google’s VarIntGB, Binary Packing and Frame-of-Reference.

arxiv-2108-12411.title: Towards a Methodology for Participant Selection in Software Engineering Experiments CCS: Software and its engineering Empirical software validation
arxiv-2108-12411.creator: Valentina Lenarduzzi, 1 Oscar Dieste, 2 Davide Fucci, 3 Sira Vegas 2
arxiv-2108-12411.description: Abstract . Background. Software Engineering (SE) researchers extensively perform experiments with human subjects. Well-defined samples are required to ensure external validity. Samples are selected purposely or by convenience , limiting the generalizability of results. Objective. We aim to depict the current status of participants selection in empirical SE, identifying the main threats and how they are mitigated.

arxiv-2109-13075.title: An Integrated Quantum Material Testbed with Multi-Resolution Photoemission Spectroscopy
arxiv-2109-13075.creator: Chenhui Yan, Emanuel Green, Riku Fukumori, Nikola Protic, Seng Huat Lee, Sebastian Fernandez-Mulligan, Rahim Raja, Robin Erdakos, Zhiqiang Mao, Shuolong Yang
arxiv-2109-13075.description: Abstract We present the development of a multi-resolution photoemission spectroscopy (MRPES) setup which probes quantum materials in energy, momentum, space, and time. This versatile setup integrates three light sources in one photoemission setup, and can conveniently switch between traditional angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), time-resolved ARPES (trARPES), and micron-scale spatially resolved ARPES ( μ \mu ARPES).

arxiv-2212-11214.title: Crowd Score: A Method for the Evaluation of Jokes using Large Language Model AI Voters as Judges
arxiv-2212-11214.creator: Fabrício Góes, Zisen Zhou, Piotr Sawicki, Marek Grzes, Daniel G. Brown
arxiv-2212-11214.description: Abstract This paper presents the Crowd Score, a novel method to assess the funniness of jokes using large language models (LLMs) as AI judges. Our method relies on inducing different personalities into the LLM and aggregating the votes of the AI judges into a single score to rate jokes.

arxiv-2402-07814.title: PBADet: A One-Stage Anchor-Free Approach for Part-Body Association
arxiv-2402-07814.creator: Zhongpai Gao, Huayi Zhou, Abhishek Sharma, Meng Zheng, Benjamin Planche, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu
arxiv-2402-07814.description: Abstract The detection of human parts ( e.g . , hands, face) and their correct association with individuals is an essential task, e.g . , for ubiquitous human-machine interfaces and action recognition. Traditional methods often employ multi-stage processes, rely on cumbersome anchor-based systems, or do not scale well to larger part sets.

arxiv-2407-14525.title: Morse Code-Enabled Speech Recognition for Individuals with Visual and Hearing Impairments
arxiv-2407-14525.creator: Ritabrata Roy Choudhury
arxiv-2407-14525.description: Abstract The proposed model aims to develop a speech recognition technology for hearing, speech, or cognitively disabled people. All the available technology in the field of speech recognition doesn’t come with an interface for communication for people with hearing, speech, or cognitive disabilities.

arxiv-2409-04816.title: Ill-posedness of the Dirichlet problem for 2D Lagrangian mean curvature equations
arxiv-2409-04816.creator: Wentao Cao, Zhehui Wang
arxiv-2409-04816.description: Abstract . We investigate the Dirichlet problem of the two-dimensional Lagrangian mean curvature equation in bounded domains. Infinitely many C 1 , α ​ ( α ∈ ( 0 , 1 5 ) ) C^{1,\alpha}(\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{5})) very weak solutions are built through Nash-Kuiper construction.

arxiv-2502-07068.title: Specializing Large Language Models to Simulate Survey Response Distributions for Global Populations
arxiv-2502-07068.creator: Yong Cao 1, Haijiang Liu 2, Arnav Arora 3, Isabelle Augenstein 3
arxiv-2502-07068.description: Abstract Large-scale surveys are essential tools for informing social science research and policy, but running surveys is costly and time-intensive. If one could accurately simulate group-level survey results, this could be very valuable to social science research. Prior work has explored the use of large language models (LLMs) for simulating human behaviors, mostly through prompting.

arxiv-2503-05870.title: Impurity-induced Mott ring states and Mott zeros ring states in the Hubbard operator formalism
arxiv-2503-05870.creator: Emile Pangburn, Anurag Banerjee, Catherine Pépin, Cristina Bena
arxiv-2503-05870.description: Abstract We study the formation of subgap impurity states in strongly correlated Mott insulators. We use a composite operator method that gives us access to both the bulk Green’s function, as well as to the real-space Green’s function in the presence of an impurity.

arxiv-2503-06996.title: Public space security management using digital twin technologies Thanks: The research leading to these results has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101073876 (Ceasefire). This publication reflects only the authors vi
arxiv-2503-06996.creator: Stylianos Zindros 1 , Christos Chronis 1 , Panagiotis Radoglou-Grammatikis 2 , Vasileios Argyriou 3, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis 2 , Iraklis Varlamis 1 , Georgios Th. Papadopoulos 1
arxiv-2503-06996.description: Abstract As the security of public spaces remains a critical issue in today’s world, Digital Twin technologies have emerged in recent years as a promising solution for detecting and predicting potential future threats. The applied methodology leverages a Digital Twin of a metro station in Athens, Greece, using the FlexSim simulation software.

arxiv-2508-09994.title: Whisper Smarter, not Harder: Adversarial Attack on Partial Suppression
arxiv-2508-09994.creator: Zheng Jie Wong, Bingquan Shen
arxiv-2508-09994.description: Abstract Currently, Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models are deployed in an extensive range of applications. However, recent studies have demonstrated the possibility of adversarial attack on these models which could potentially suppress or disrupt model output. We investigate and verify the robustness of these attacks and explore if it is possible to increase their imperceptibility.

arxiv-2602-00714.creator: Xue Ren, Ran Zhang

plos-pone-0009722.creator: Rahul Siddharthan
plos-pone-0009722.description: PLOS ONE research article. Dinucleotide Weight Matrices for Predicting Transcription Factor Binding Sites: Generalizing the Position Weight Matrix

pmc-11382051.title: Multi-omics reveals protective effects of Ling Gui Zhu Gan Decoction on hyperlipidaemia in hamster
pmc-11382051.creator: Baolin Li, Qi Qian, Liying Niu, Xinguo Wang
pmc-11382051.description: Ling Gui Zhu Gan decoction (LGZGD) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) prescription that is widely used in cardiovascular disease clinical prevention and treatment with high efficacy. Recent studies have shown that LGZGD can also be used in hyperlipidemia (HL) intervention, but its pharmacodynamic material basis and its mechanisms remains unclear.

pmc-11456590.title: Cooperative dynamics of PARP-1 zinc-finger domains in the detection of DNA single-strand breaks
pmc-11456590.creator: Parvathy A. P. Sarma, Corinne Abbadie, Fabrizio Cleri
pmc-11456590.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The DNA single-strand break (SSB) repair pathway is initiated by the multifunctional enzyme PARP-1, which recognizes the broken DNA ends by its two zinc-finger domains, Zn1 and Zn2. Despite a number of experiments performed with different DNA configurations and reduced fragments of PARP-1, many details of this interaction that is crucial to the correct initiation of the repair chain are still unclear.

pmc-11528109.title: Influence of geographic isolation and the environment on gene flow among phenotypically diverse lizards
pmc-11528109.creator: Thomas J McGreevy, Nicholas G Crawford, Pierre Legreneur, Christopher J Schneider
pmc-11528109.description: Lizards in the genus Anolis comprise hundreds of species that display a wide range of phenotypic variation closely related to their environment. One example is the Guadeloupean anole (Anolis marmoratus ssp.) that display extreme phenotypic variation, primarily in adult male color and pattern, with twelve described subspecies on the archipelago.

pmc-12489827.title: A structured institutional framework for establishing a living allogenic valve transplant program
pmc-12489827.creator: Muhammad Faateh, Muhammad Aanish Raees, Yacmet Colón Berríos, Amra Zekic, Hosam F Ahmed, Tara Karamlou, James F Cnota, Benjamin S Mantell, David LS Morales, Awais Ashfaq
pmc-12489827.description: Living allogenic valve transplantation (LAVT) refers to transplantation of viable human heart valves in an orthotopic or heterotopic fashion and has recently garnered significant interest for children in need of a living, growing, regenerating valve replacement option. However, at present, there is no standardized approach for establishing and implementing such a program.

pmc-12500988.title: Building a coronavirus disease 2019 healthcare registry in an evolving pandemic
pmc-12500988.creator: Indumathi Venkatachalam, Edwin Philip Conceicao, Jean Xiang Ying Sim, Shalvi Arora, Yue Yang, Jin Yee Shoon, Yingqi Xu, Marcus Eng Hock Ong, Sze Ling Chan
pmc-12500988.description: COVID-19 emerged in Wuhan, China in December 2019 and was declared a pandemic on March 11, 2020. As there were many unknowns about COVID-19, an immediate priority early in the pandemic was to collect high-quality data to understand disease characteristics and epidemiology to inform healthcare resource management.

pmc-12640233.title: Assessing a peer-led pain and wellness self-management program with older adults
pmc-12640233.creator: Erin Hou, Maddy Hatch, Gretchen D Tanbonliong, Dorothea K Vafiadis, John A Guidry
pmc-12640233.description: Background and ObjectivesIn 2021, the National Council on Aging developed the Self-Management Curriculum for Wellness and Pain Relief (NCWPR), a peer-based pain self-management program that provides person-centered pain management strategies, credible information on pain management methods and medications, and safe practices for the use of OTC drugs.

pmc-12656546.title: Enterohepatic Recirculation-Mediated Reabsorption of Aristolochic Acid I: Revealed by Toxicokinetics and Metabolite Identification in Rats
pmc-12656546.creator: Lieyan Huang, Lixing Nie, Xiao Ye, Zhi Lin, Ying Liu, Feng Wei
pmc-12656546.description: Aristolochic acid I (AAI) is widely recognized as a genotoxic and cytotoxic compound. To rationally propose detoxification strategies, it is essential to fully elucidate the in vivo disposition of AAI. Nevertheless, the toxicokinetic characteristics of AAI, particularly the possible involvement of the recirculation process, remain incompletely understood.

pmc-12773405.title: Abstract 103: Acute Onset Rhythmic Tremor In Acute Frontal Cortical Infarction: A Case Report
pmc-12773405.creator: JoBeth D Bingham, Thomas Chelimsky, Shital Patel
pmc-12773405.description: IntroductionAcute ischemic stroke varies in presentation, and it is crucial to quickly identify patients presenting with stroke for timely intervention. Secondary movement disorders occurring after a delayed period following ischemic stroke have been well‐documented, though rare. Holmes tremor specifically has been described as a delayed result of ischemic infarction involving subcortical structures such as mollaret triangle, thalamus, and basal ganglia.

pmc-12815772.title: Fostering learning among the next generation of veterinarians: incorporating one health and antimicrobial stewardship into veterinary medicine training curricula in Ethiopia
pmc-12815772.creator: Ndungu Nyokabi, Lisette Phelan, Stefan Berg, Johanna Lindahl, Lilian Korir, Bernard Bett, Emmanuel Muunda, Adane Mihret, Henrietta Moore, James Wood
pmc-12815772.description: Universities play a crucial role in educating and training veterinarians, and their fostering of learning among the next generation of students is widely regarded as key to bringing about the cultural change required to realise a transition towards a ‘One Health’ approach to managing human, animal, and environmental health and underpin widespread adoption of antimicrobial stewardship practices.

pmc-12822118.title: Efficacy and safety of telitacicept in the treatment of immunoglobulin a nephropathy: a real-world, single-center, retrospective study
pmc-12822118.creator: Lunju Luo, Yiyao Deng, Shuang Chen, Yuqi Yang, Lu Liu, Rui Zhang, Zhengsheng Li, Lu Yang, Yan Zha, Jing Yuan
pmc-12822118.description: BackgroundImmunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), the most common glomerular disease, is characterized by immune complex deposition and abnormal complement system activation. Telitacicept targets B cells through multiple mechanisms, potentially offering therapeutic benefits in IgAN. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of telitacicept.

pmc-13079528.title: Intersectionality in Weight Stigma Research: A Systematic Review of Empirical Evidence
pmc-13079528.creator: Abdul-Hanan Saani Inusah, Menglin Shang, Xiaoming Li, Shan Qiao
pmc-13079528.description: BackgroundSocial stigma and discrimination based on body weight or size (weight stigma) contribute to inequities in healthcare access, yet research often treats weight stigma as a uniform exposure. Intersectionality has been invoked to address this limitation by situating weight stigma within intersecting systems of power and marginalization. However, how intersectionality is operationalized in empirical weight stigma research remains unclear.

pmc-13254956.title: The impact of integrated care on quality of life in community-dwelling older adults with frailty: A systematic review and mixed method synthesis
pmc-13254956.creator: Joanne Boyce, Declan Patton, Chanel Watson, Tom O’Connor, Zena Moore, Linda Nugent
pmc-13254956.description: BackgroundFrailty among older adults is an escalating public health challenge, often associated with poorer quality of life (QoL) and increased pressure on healthcare systems. Integrated care is proposed as a strategy to meet the complex needs of this population, though evidence of its effectiveness remains inconclusive.

pmc-13296107.title: Perioperative neurofilament light chain and glial fibrillary acidic protein as biomarkers of postoperative delirium: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13296107.creator: Yan-Wu Yang, Yan Zhang, Tian-Yi Qu, Jing Yu, Zhi Wan, Mei-Ling Ge
pmc-13296107.description: BackgroundPostoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious neurocognitive complication reflecting acute brain dysfunction and predicting long-term cognitive decline. Neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) are biomarkers of neuronal and astroglial injury, but their relevance to POD remains uncertain.

pmc-13427538.title: Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Rotigotine Safety in PKD
pmc-13427538.creator: Audrey Dumont, Adrien Cour, Muriel Quillard-Murraine, Margaux Van Wynsberghe, Sophie Ruault, Sabrina Prod’Homme, Estelle Houivet, Gabriel Choukroun, Cédric Renard, Clémence Béchade, Amandine Claudinot, François Glowacki, Philippe Puech, Nell Marty, Virginie Buchbach, Nathalie Donnadieu, Elise Duhamel, Jean-Nicolas Dacher, Dominique Guerrot, Jérémy Bellien

pmc-13437799.title: FGF/FGFR signaling at the immune-stromal interface in autoimmune rheumatic diseases: from tissue remodeling to translational opportunities
pmc-13437799.creator: Sheng Zhong, Xiaohui Meng, Zheng Xiang, Guowei Qiu, Songtao Sun, Jun Xie, Lianbo Xiao
pmc-13437799.description: The fibroblast growth factor (FGF)/FGF receptor (FGFR) signaling system regulates tissue repair, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, fibrosis, and bone metabolism. Although FGF/FGFR biology has been extensively studied in oncology, development, and fibrotic lung disease, its relevance to systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases remains scattered across disease-specific and unevenly supported literatures.

pmc-13521805.title: Relation of climatic exposures with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy in a two-center retrospective cohort
pmc-13521805.creator: Xiao Chen, Chang Zou, Yang Liu, Ruru Zhao, Hanxiang Sun, Xiaosong Liu, Qinxin Shen, Yuanyuan Yang, Qiaoling Du
pmc-13521805.description: ObjectiveTo investigate relation between climatic exposures and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) in Chinese cities Shanghai and Sanya.BackgroundICP is a pregnancy-specific liver disease associated with adverse fetal outcomes. Although the etiology of ICP remains unclear, climatic exposures are increasingly recognized as one of the critical correlates in ICP onset.

pmc-13525180.title: No Clear Evidence of Histopathological Effects Linked to NSAIDs in the Kidney or Liver of Fish Exposed to Treated Municipal Wastewaters
pmc-13525180.creator: Johanna Näslund, Leif Norrgren, D. G. Joakim Larsson
pmc-13525180.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can cause histopathological changes in the kidney and liver of fish. Still, it is unclear whether exposure to treated municipal wastewater that contains NSAID residues causes similar effects. We therefore conducted a comprehensive, critical review on claimed histopathological changes in fish exposed either to NSAIDs or to treated municipal wastewater in the laboratory or downstream from treatment plants. A detailed scrutinization questioned the basis for several findings.

pmc-13542424.title: Co-incubation of Bacillus spp. alleviated the growth and gas production of potentially harmful bacteria in different in vitro methodologies
pmc-13542424.creator: Lena Capern, Nina Milora, Emily George, Audrey Segura, Raphaele Gresse, Oscar Queiroz, Giuseppe Copani, Bruno I. Cappellozza
pmc-13542424.description: Graphical AbstractSummary: Potentially harmful bacteria are known to affect the health and performance of dairy cows and calves, whereas Bacillus-based direct-fed microbials have been shown to support the health and performance of the dairy cattle herd via distinct modes of action. pmc-13609503.title: Intragraft FOXP3+ Cells and Continuous Banff Indices in T Cell-Mediated Kidney Allograft Rejection
pmc-13609503.creator: Petar Đolonga, Petar Šenjug, Anja Stadnik, Ana Dunatov Huljev, Lada Zibar, Sandra Zekić Tomaš, Danica Galešić Ljubanović, Merica Glavina Durdov
pmc-13609503.description: Background and Objectives: FOXP3+ (Forkhead box P3) regulatory T cells contribute to immune tolerance after kidney transplantation, but their role in T cell-mediated rejection (TCMR) remains controversial. This study investigated the association between intragraft FOXP3+ cells and the recently introduced Banff-derived activity (AI) and chronicity index (CI) in biopsy-proven TCMR.
